style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a weathered concrete surface, extreme asymmetric off-centre left framing with generous negative space on the right. Three recognisable engineered parts: a heavy brass time-clock gear mechanism, a latched inspection cover, and a solid steel limit block physically stopping the gear's rotation. Hard clean edges, one directional key light from above throwing a long cast shadow to the right. Matte muted palette of industrial grey and oxidized brass. No bare geometry, no text, no molded lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, UI, watermarks, floating shapes
rationale: The story is about a structural, mathematical ceiling on compensation. A component assembly physically materializes this abstract threshold as a mechanical limit stop.
cue: Your raise dies at about 51.5 hours
subject: A modular mechanical time-clock assembly hitting a physical steel limit stop
core_thesis: Federal pay tables assume a 40-hour week, but actual hours push the hourly value of a manager's salary down to a developer's rate at 51.5 hours.
core_conflict: Fixed salary compensation versus uncapped actual hours worked.
